advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add or reference regression coverage for the plan-review paths (`_verifier_cfg` verifier sub-calls, prerequisites escalation ladder) that `_effective_config` newly activates, or confirm with the operator that the plan-review behavior change is intended and verified.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/runner.py:272 `cfg = _effective_config(self._config, req)` — the shared runner's entry point, reached by every gate
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/xcheck.py:198 `vcfg = _verifier_cfg(cfg)` and :336 — verifier sub-calls that pass a divergent config to a runner built with cfg.model

ticket b690 comment: 'of 22 RunRequest construction sites... FOUR deliberately pass a config DIFFERENT from the one their runner was built with — and all four were therefore silently ineffective... Every one is in plan-review' and 'it IS a live behaviour change to the plan-review gate'

ABSENCE: the 4 new test files under tests/unit and tests/unit/workflow exercise only code-review.yaml; no test in this diff runs plan-review to confirm the newly-activated _verifier_cfg / ladder behavior is correct
advisory.finding: `_effective_config` lives in the shared `PydanticAIRunner`, so it activates per-call model overrides in EVERY gate that sets `req.config.model` — not only code-review. In plan-review this newly makes `_verifier_cfg` (xcheck.py:198,336; __init__.py:160) and the prerequisites size-escalation ladder take effect for the first time (moving Pass-2 verifier sub-calls off the frontier model and enabling ladder escalation), a live behavior change. This diff adds regression tests only for the code-review path; none guard the plan-review paths the same fix now changes.
scenarios: A plan-review run whose Pass-2 verifier verdict previously depended on running on the frontier model now runs on the cheaper standard/verifier model and may decide differently.
A large plan's prerequisite pass now escalates on context-limit errors where it previously retried the same model.

advisory.finding: The documented `not requested` (empty-string / absent) model fallback branch of `_effective_config` is untested — only the `requested == base.model` half of the OR-guard is exercised, so a refactor dropping the empty-model clause would silently break the stated direct-library-caller contract ('substituting an empty model would build a provider session for nothing and fail deep inside the SDK').
